You must always use the taste-skill rules (design-taste-frontend) for any frontend, UI, or design-related task. This includes creating landing pages, components, layouts, hero sections, forms, navigation, pricing tables, or any visual interface.

Follow these rules strictly:

\- Never generate AI-purple gradients, mesh blobs, or slop patterns.

\- Never use em-dashes (—) or en-dashes (–) in UI copy; use hyphens (-) or rewrite the sentence.

\- Never generate three-equal-card feature rows; use asymmetric grids, zig-zag layouts, or scroll-pinned alternatives.

\- Never add scroll cues, decorative status dots, version footers, or "BETA/INVITE-ONLY" labels on marketing pages.

\- Always ship dual-mode (light + dark) by default with WCAG AA contrast.

\- One accent color across the whole page. One corner-radius system per page.

\- Hero must fit initial viewport: headline max 2 lines, subtext max 20 words, primary CTA visible without scroll.

\- Read the brief first, infer the right design direction (layout variance, motion, density) before writing any code.

The SKILL.md file is already installed globally at ~/.copilot/skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md. Refer to it for the full rule set.
